review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the neighbouring ConvexFlag/Basic.lean (simp lemma `mem_domain`, defs `EvaluableAt`, `eval`, `ConvexCombination`) and grepped the project for uses of the weak-hull API. `weakConvexHull_idempotent` and `mem_weakConvexHull_iff` are not used outside this file. Helly.lean unfolds `weakConvexHull` directly (`unfold weakConvexHull at h`) rather than through a lemma. The only simp-interface defect I could support from the sources is the unmarked idempotence lemma. I did not recommend a simp attribute on `mem_weakConvexHull_iff`, because its `∃ hs` and dependent-proof statement would expand membership goals unhelpfully. I did not recommend one on `subset_weakConvexHull` or on the monotonicity and absorption lemmas, because they are conditional or non-equational. I ran no Lean, so this is untested.

findings.problem: This is a closure-operator idempotence equation. Its left side is strictly larger than its right side, and it has no hypotheses, so it is a canonical terminating simp rewrite. It is not tagged `@[simp]`. Any goal or hypothesis containing a doubly nested `F.weakConvexHull (F.weakConvexHull S)` is not normalised by `simp`. Mathlib marks the analogous `ClosureOperator.idempotent` as simp. The hull API here (`subset_weakConvexHull`, `weakConvexHull_mono`, `weakConvexHull_absorb`, `weakConvexHull_idempotent`) has the shape of a closure operator, but it has no simp-normal form for nested hulls. Downstream uses in Helly.lean manage hull inclusions by hand (e.g. `weakConvexHull_absorb (hreplacementSubset k hki) hk`).
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `weakConvexHull_idempotent`, which gives `@[simp] theorem weakConvexHull_idempotent (F : ConvexFlag) (S : Set F.Point) : ...`. This is safe: the rewrite strictly decreases term size, so it cannot cycle, and the lemma has no side conditions. Do not also tag `weakConvexHull_absorb`, which is conditional and has a non-equational conclusion.
findings.benefit: `simp` will collapse nested weak hulls to the canonical single hull. This matches how Mathlib's closure operators behave, and it removes the need to cite the lemma by hand wherever hulls get nested.
